section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions how the maamar's reference to "peace from above to below and from below to above" can apply to both types of birurim, given that birur from below to above is usually associated with war, not peace.
section.t: And seemingly it must be said,
that the intention
(in the maamar)
in "from above to below and from below to above" is
(also)
for the two manners in the matter of the birurim
(the matter of "veshavti,"
the return of the sparks to their source),
birur by way of from above to below and birur by way of from below to above.
And it needs to be understood,
behold it is explained in many places
[and also in the aforementioned maamar
(beginning "Padeh BeShalom")
of the Master of the Redemption,
brought above in sections 1-2],
that the matter of peace is in the birur by way of from above to below
(birur through the revelation of light),
but not so the birur that is by way of from below to above
(birur by way of enclothing)
is in a manner of war,
and from this that it says that the explanation of "BeShalom" is two peaces,
peace from above to below and peace from below to above,
it implies that also the birur from below to above is in a manner of peace.
And to add,
from this that it is said "and I will return in peace" two peaces
(that both must be),
it implies,
that in each one of them there is an advantage.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in birur from above to below the opposing entity is nullified, while in birur from below to above the lower entity is clarified through its own will and its opposition remains latent.
section.t: e)
And the matter is,
that in peace
(that is made through the birur)
there are two manners.
That the opposing [entity] is nullified – and this manner is
(primarily)
in the birur by way of from above to below.
For in the birur by way of from below to above,
where the clarifier enclothes in the clarified and engages with it so that it will desire to be clarified,
this is not that the lower [entity]
(the clarified)
is nullified, but rather it is clarified from its own will.
And since even after it is clarified it is an existence of a lower [entity]
(for lower and higher are opposites),
therefore,
even after it is clarified,
it is possible that it will oppose the higher.
And in the service of man it is,
that the birur of the Nefesh HaBahamis through the Nefesh HaElokis enclothing itself in the Nefesh HaBahamis,
is,
that the contemplation of the Nefesh HaElokis is in a manner that also the Nefesh HaBahamis will understand and grasp the G-dly matter
(that it contemplates)
through which it will come to love HaShem.
For this that the Nefesh HaBahamis loves HaShem
(although by its nature it is drawn to physical matters)
is
(not through its existence being nullified,
but rather on the contrary)
through the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis coming to an understanding that one must love HaShem.
And since this that the Nefesh HaBahamis loves HaShem
(including also the understanding and comprehension that one must love HaShem)
is from the intellect of the Nefesh HaElokis
(that enclothed in the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis),
but the Nefesh HaBahamis in its own essence is drawn to physical matters
[and as explained in many places
that the birur of the Nefesh HaBahamis through contemplation is only in the manner of itkafya],
behold even now
(that also the Nefesh HaBahamis has love of HaShem)
the opposition of it to the Nefesh HaElokis remains in concealment
(only that its opposition does not come into actuality).
And in order that there be nullification of the opposing [entity], it is through the birur by way of from above to below.
For through
that there is revealed in the lower [entity] a revelation of light that is not in proportion to it,
it is nullified from its existence.
And in the service of man it is,
that through the love of the Nefesh HaElokis that is above intellect and comprehension being felt in the Nefesh HaBahamis,
for this love is
(generally)
a great love that is above the limitation of the vessel of the heart,
through this the existence of the Nefesh HaBahamis is nullified,
and through this it is transformed to good,
ithapcha
(which is above itkafya).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in birur from below to above the former opponent becomes a lover, whereas in birur from above to below the lower entity is nullified but its own existence is not fundamentally changed.
section.t: And another manner in peace
(that is made through the birur),
that that which was initially opposing becomes a lover
(and in the language of the verse
"even his enemies will make peace with him")
– and this manner is
(primarily)
in the birur by way of from below to above.
For in the birur by way of from above to below,
this that the lower [entity] does not oppose is because it is nullified from its existence through the revelation of light,
but it is not that a change is made in the existence of the lower [entity] itself.
For although through the revelation of the great love that is above intellect and comprehension the Nefesh HaBahamis is transformed to good
(ithapcha),
behold the ithapcha of it is
(not from the aspect of the essence of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
but rather)
because through the great love of the Nefesh HaElokis the Nefesh HaBahamis is nullified from its existence.
And the true matter of "even his enemies will make peace with him" is in the birur by way of from below to above,
for this that the Nefesh HaBahamis has love of HaShem is from the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis.
